mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not higher than baseline during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, which may lead to economic downturns and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment (PAYEMS) alongside rising GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which should drive positive equity returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not positively correlated with joint PAYEMS and GDPC1 growth (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth (INDPRO) above 2% annually signals strong supply-side activity, which supports equity market growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not higher when INDPRO exceeds 2% growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) increasing at a rate above historical averages indicates strong consumer demand, which should positively impact equity markets.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not positively correlated with HOUST growth (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Slowing payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) signals potential economic weakness, leading to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases when PAYEMS growth slows.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) combined with low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) indicates inflationary pressures that may erode equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not negatively correlated with joint CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS movements (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Retail and food services sales (RSAFS) increasing above 5% annually signals strong consumer spending, which supports equity market growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not higher when RSAFS exceeds 5% growth (t-test p > 0.05).
